title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
description: Narrate or write news stories, reviews, or commentary for print, broadcast, or other communications media such as newspapers, magazines, radio, or television. May collect and analyze information through interview, investigation, or observation.

tasks.text: Research a story's background information to provide complete and accurate information.
Gather information and develop perspectives about news subjects through research, interviews, observation, and experience.
Investigate breaking news developments, such as disasters, crimes, or human-interest stories.
Report on specialized fields such as medicine, green technology, environmental issues, science, politics, sports, arts, consumer affairs, business, religion, crime, or education.
Check reference materials, such as books, news files, or public records, to obtain relevant facts.
Take pictures or video, and process them for inclusion in a story.
Conduct taped or filmed interviews or narratives.
Develop ideas or material for columns or commentaries by analyzing and interpreting news, current issues, or personal experiences.
Examine news items of local, national, and international significance to determine topics to address, or obtain assignments from editorial staff members.
Analyze and interpret news and information received from various sources to broadcast the information.
Receive assignments or evaluate leads or tips to develop story ideas.
Select material most pertinent to presentation, and organize this material into appropriate formats.
Revise work to meet editorial approval or to fit time or space requirements.
Review and evaluate notes taken about news events to isolate pertinent facts and details.
Review written, audio, or video copy, and correct errors in content, grammar, or punctuation, following prescribed editorial style and formatting guidelines.
Determine a published or broadcasted story's emphasis, length, and format, organizing material accordingly.
Write commentaries, columns, or scripts, using computers.
Transmit news stories or reporting information from remote locations, using equipment such as satellite phones, telephones, fax machines, or modems.
Photograph or videotape news events.
Write online blog entries that address news developments or offer additional information, opinions, or commentary on news events.
Write columns, editorials, commentaries, or reviews that interpret events or offer opinions.
Coordinate and serve as an anchor on news broadcast programs.
Arrange interviews with people who can provide information about a story.
Present news stories, and introduce in-depth videotaped segments or live transmissions from on-the-scene reporters.
Establish and maintain relationships with individuals who are credible sources of information.
Report news stories for publication or broadcast, describing the background and details of events.
Discuss issues with editors to establish priorities or positions.
Present live or recorded commentary via broadcast media.
Communicate with readers, viewers, advertisers, or the general public via mail, email, or telephone.
Assign stories to other reporters or duties to production staff.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook, Social media sites, Social media software, Web content management system CMS software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: FileMaker Pro, Microsoft Access, Microsoft SQL Server, Online databases.

skills.name: Video creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to enable production of video content. Examples: Adobe After Effects, Adobe Premiere Pro, Apple Final Cut Pro, Grass Valley EDIUS.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics, Nielsen Arianna, Nielsen Marketbreaks, Statistical analysis software.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign, Microsoft Publisher, QuarkXPress.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Photoshop.
